source_title: Liam Neeson Reveals Kangaroos Nearly Disrupted Filming of His New Action Movie in Australia (Exclusive) - People.com
source_excerpt:
The actor stars in action-thriller ‘The Mongoose’, in theaters today
Liam Neeson says kangaroos created safety concerns during dusk drives from the Australian set of The Mongoose
Director Mark Vanselow had to keep kangaroos from entering car-action scenes during filming
The Mongoose stars Neeson and Marisa Tomei and arrives in theaters today
Liam Neeson had some unexpected visitors while filming his latest movie.
In an exclusive interview with PEOPLE for his action thriller The Mongoose , the Schindler’s List star, 74, alongside director and longtime stunt double Mark Vanselow , shares that filming in Australia meant watching out for some unexpected guests: kangaroos.
“We saw a lot of them, yeah. Especially at dusk, driving back from set,” Neeson says. “It could be very dangerous. You don’t know when they’re going to hop across the road.”
After working as Neeson’s stunt double for decades, including serving as his butt double in the 2014 comedy A Million Ways to Die in the West , Vanselow takes the director’s seat for his first feature with The Mongoose .
The film stars Neeson alongside Marisa Tomei , whom he calls a “wonderful actress” who raised his game on set . Neeson plays Ryan “Fang” Flanagan, a decorated combat veteran on the run from police after being accused of murder. The role sends the Oscar-nominated Irish actor, who tells PEOPLE he’s “just not into cars,” on a high-speed chase across the country in a Shelby Super Snake.
Vanselow shares that the kangaroos posed a challenge during the film’s car scenes.
“We had a track that we were doing some of the car action on, and the kangaroos were everywhere,” he says. “So we had to watch out for them and make sure they didn’t hop in front of the vehicles while we were shooting.”

Beyond the danger, the kangaroos also posed a major plot hole. While The Mongoose was shot in Australia, its story takes place in Kentucky, Arkansas and Texas.
“And especially because we shot it in Melbourne and Melbourne surrounds. The movie’s supposed to be set in America. So to have a kangaroo in shot, no, that wouldn’t be good,” Neeson says.
